_note: LEVEL 4-32's DARK DRAGON - entity `dark_dragon.ent`, spawned by `dark_dragon_spawn`,
role `boss_spawn`. The fourth boss, the last level of the game, and the last thing in
this remaster.
THE WHOLE LEVEL, decoded end to end, because every piece of it is one mechanism:
1. level31c is `darkest` and holds an unlit torch (`light_off`, 210 34). Shooting it
lights it - which takes the LIGHT WALL away (Torch.hpp, already built) and, in the
same act, adds a `light_from_projectile.ent`.
2. `dark_dragon_spawn` waits 3000 ms, sees that light, and marks ITSELF destroyed.
3. 4000 ms later it adds `dark_dragon.ent` at its own place, calls
breakDarkDragonWall, starts the music, and deletes itself.
4. The dragon hovers in, settles at `fighting`, and shoots fireballs at the player.
5. The player portals the BARREL BOMB - `teleportable = 1` - into the line of fire.
The dragon's own fireball detonates it, and the blast BURNS the dragon.
6. Each wound: hp -1, a red flash, YOUR PORTALS ARE TAKEN AWAY, and as it ends a
shot at the torch ONLY IF `light_off.ent` exists - a torch its fire signal put out
- which relights it (damage note). Each shot at the player restocks the barrel bomb
when none is left (`restock` below; built in planning step 116).
7. At hp 0 it falls and drops a YELLOW KEY at `key_pos` and a platform at
`platform_pos`. The key opens the yellow door, and the door is the way to the exit.
THE BOSS SUPPLIES BOTH ITS OWN AMMUNITION AND ITS OWN DETONATOR, and that is not a
reading - addEntityIfItCantBeFound restocks `barrel_bomb` after every shot it takes, and
the port's own fireball path (Game.cpp) already asks an overlapping bomb to go off. The
level places no fire agent and no fire diamond, so the dragon's fireball is the ONLY
thing in level31c that can light the only thing that can hurt it.
THE LEVEL, measured from level31c.tscn: 768 x 256 px (`max` at (768, 256)) - an arena,
where level31a's dragon had 2632 px to chase you down. main_char (710, 48), door.ent
(704, 176), dark_dragon_spawn (-144, 210) off the left edge, shout (-4, 140), fighting
(16, 56), breakable_wall (32, 128), light_off (210, 34) with switch = 1, light_wall.ent
(64, 240), key_pos (78, 208), platform_pos (160, 240), barrel_spawn (430, 0),
barrel_bomb (430, 63), keyhole.ent (592, 200) yellow, door_locked.ent (624, 160) yellow.
properties: darkest = 1, no_music = 1. NO auto_camera - that is level31a's alone.
ETHCallback_dark_dragon_spawn, bytes 388631..389418. Two arms on isDestroyed(), which
(MiscCallbacks 347456..347560) is nothing but a `destroy` custom uint - destroy() sets
it and deletes nothing.
NOT destroyed:  elapsedTime > 3000 && SeekEntity("light_from_projectile.ent") != null
-> destroy(this); elapsedTime = 0
destroyed:      elapsedTime > 4000 && !isFinished
-> AddScaledEntity("dark_dragon.ent", spawnPoint.GetPosition())
breakDarkDragonWall(); playGameMusic(true)
playDarkDragonAppearSound(); DeleteEntity(this)
WHAT THE PORT WATCHES INSTEAD, and why it is the same event. The light entity is added
by ETHCallback_light_off (467198..467878): while unlit the torch spins and calls
hasProjectileAround(pos, 24), and a projectile within that adds
`light_from_projectile.ent`. That is exactly the condition Torch already decodes and
already counts - Torch::State::lit - so the port reads `lit > 0` rather than modelling
an entity whose only purpose is to be sought by name.
ONE DIVERGENCE, STATED: Torch is a TOGGLE, and `lit` here is monotonic - it counts
torches lit over the level's life and never comes back down. So a player who lit the
torch and shot the flame out again within the 3000 ms window would, in the original,
leave no light for the marker to find and disarm the summon; here the arming stands.
Recorded rather than built: it is a three-second race against oneself, in a level whose
torch is also the only way to see, and a port that modelled it would have to model the
light entity's own lifetime, which nothing else in the game reads.
breakDarkDragonWall (398405..398575) seeks `breakable_wall` and calls destroy on it.
level31c's breakable_wall_2217 carries metadata/breakable = 1, so it is ALREADY a
Demolish::Breakable with a body the port tracks - the removal goes through Demolish
exactly as the torch's light wall does, and the two are different bodies that never
meet. This level is the only one in the game that holds both kinds of wall.
dark_dragon.ent, read from the extracted entities (never copied here): type 0,
static 0, shape 2, sensor 1, density 0, gravityScale 0, Collision Size 220 x 220, and
custom data carrying `burnable`.
A SENSOR WITH NO SOLID BODY, so it cannot touch the player and the player cannot stand
on it - the ghost's shape, and the reason this module keeps a position rather than an
entity. It is also why the port tests the blast against it explicitly: Fire::Blast
matches candidates by body, and this boss has none, as Game does for the ghost against a
blast since planning step 117 (Ghost::BlastReaches).
`burnable` is what makes the barrel bomb the weapon. The blast's own filter is
isBreakableOrExplosiveOrBurnable, so the dragon is in the set it grabs.
radius_px is HALF of the 220 x 220 Collision. The original grabs with a sphere of
blast.radius_px against that real box; the port tests a distance against this radius
plus the blast's own, which is the same test with the box approximated by its half
extent. hp is NOT in the .ent - the callback writes 3 on its first tick.
ETHCallback_dark_dragon, bytes 389418..397662 - 8.2 KB and ~2178 instructions, the
largest callback in the game. States: APPEARING 0, FIGHTING 2, DAMAGE 3, DYING 4.
THE FIRE INTERVAL SHORTENS AS IT IS HURT, tested every tick against the live hp:
if (hp <= 2) fireInterval -= 600;  if (hp <= 1) fireInterval -= 600;
so 4200, then 3600, then 3000. It gets faster exactly as you get closer.
FIRING, when elapsedTime > fireInterval and !isFinished: GetClosestContact(dragon ->
char), and the shot happens only if the closest thing is the character - the same sight
gate as level31a's dragon, and asked the same way round here for the same reason
(Shot::FirstBody cannot return a capsule; dragon.json carries that decode). The muzzle
is scale(95) along the aim, addFireball carries killMainCharacter, and each shot brings
startEarthquake(15) and the barrel restock.
THE ANGLE, decoded (00_order 8.8, decode/D7.md section 4 with D7_check.md; the
visuals plan's 12.1, planning step 99). ins 343-356 build Follower(V2_ZERO, 800, 150),
which lags an ANGLE IN RADIANS carried in x (sim/Follower). It is not updated in
APPEARING. Entering FIGHTING (ins 665-682) it is forced to rad(GetAngle() + 360) -
APPEARING's last waypoint angle is -12, so the head is written 348 and does not swing
through a whole turn toward a target near 360 - and updated once. Each FIGHTING update
(ins 688-732): update() unless paused, THEN setDestinationPos((computeDarkDragonAngle,
0)), then SetAngle(radianToDegree(getPos().x)). computeDarkDragonAngle (398213..398405)
is getAngle(normalize(dragonPos - charPos)) + PIb x 1.2 - the DRAGON LESS the
character, and NO CLAMP: 378 - phi degrees for a character phi below it to the right.
getAngle is atan2(x, y), x first, wrapped into [0, 2 PI) (GameMath.h:711-715). Back
from DAMAGE (ins 1752-1768) the Follower is forced to rad(GetAngle()) with no turn
added. The character is SeekEntity('dark_mage.ent'), the player (ins 377-388).
THE NECK (ins 734-818): neckAdjustElapsedTime counts in FIGHTING only and is zeroed at
the init and at a wound (ins 1491-1502); bias = clamp((365 - A) / 25, 0, 1) on the
SMOOTHED angle A; lift = (smoothBothSides(bias) x 2 - 1) x scale(18) x min(neck / 2000,
1), added to originalPos - the point the NEXT update's linearMotion stands the entity
at. So the neck moves the dragon, not only its head: the blast is measured to that
point and the shots leave from it.
THE MUZZLE (ins 913-978): a = rad(-GetAngle() - 110 + 29), fireBallPos = dragonPos -
scale(95) x normalize(sin a, -cos a) - the mouth, turned with the head (level31a's
dragon has the same arithmetic, dragon.json) - and the shot flies
normalize(charPos - fireBallPos): FROM THE MOUTH, AT THE LIVE PLAYER. The sight gate
is GetClosestContact(dragonPos, charPos), from the dragon's own point.
THE MOUTH'S FIRE (ins 829-847): KillParticleSystem(0) every update while elapsedTime <
fireInterval / 2, PlayParticleSystem(0) every update while it is > fireInterval / 4 x
3, both uint arithmetic; neither between. The fire clock is NOT zeroed entering
FIGHTING: APPEARING zeroes it on every update of the jaw's leg (ins 580-591) and it
runs on through the last two legs, 2900 ms, so the first shot comes about 1.3 s into
FIGHTING (F16: the pose by 14.05 s, the shot at 15.27 s).
HURT ONLY BY FIRE, exactly as the ghost is: isBurned(dragon) -> DAMAGE, hp -1,
healBurn, playDarkDragonDamageSound. burn/isBurned/healBurn (419710..420017) are a
plain `burned` custom uint, read AFTER the mouth and the shot (ins 1067) and, like
them, only while the level is not finished (ins 821-827): so a blast on the update it
fires lets that shot leave, and a wound below half the interval enters DAMAGE with the
mouth killed. The port reads it there too (planning step 99's fix round; it read it
first before).
_fireball_particle_scale_source: addFireball's fourth argument, fireballScale. Every other caller passes 1 - the carranca
(#108 in carrancaCallback), burnProjectile (#54) and level31a's dragon (PshC4 1f at
ETHCallback_dragon #708) - and the dark dragon passes 2 at both of its calls (PshC4 2f
at #972 before #978, and at #1714 before #1720). addFireball #77-83 uses it only when it
is not 1, and then only as ScaleParticleSystem(0, fireballScale): it scales the FIRST
particle system of fireball.ent, on top of the entity's own <Scale> of 1.2, and touches
neither the light nor the halo nor the entity. So this dragon's fire is drawn at 2.4
times the .ent's particle size where every other fireball is drawn at 1.2.

TWO THINGS IN IT ARE NOT PRESENTATION:
- PortalManager::killAll, at the moment it is wounded. Every portal you have placed
is taken away. In the port that is placed.clear() and flight.reset(); the budget and
portalsUsed are deliberately left alone, because killing portals is not a refund.
- At the LAST waypoint it seeks `light_off.ent` and, ONLY if it finds one, fires a
fireball at it (ins 1615-1720; the guard is ins 1675-1694): from its MOUTH at the
angle it holds, along the line from its own point to the light's. SeekEntity
compares names exactly (ETHBucketManager.cpp:394-406); level31c places its torch
as bare `light_off` (entity 1689), a lit torch deletes itself (ETHCallback_light_off
ins 1-35, 105-114), and only ETHCallback_fire_signal adds a `light_off.ent` - the
torch put out again. So the original never fires at a LIT torch: it fires at one
its fire signal put out, and hasProjectileAround counts `fireball.ent` by name
within scale(24) of it (includeFireballs true, 467878..468609), so the shot RELIGHTS
it (the decode plus the geometry: the port's arithmetic puts the shot 1.8 u from the
torch from F16's floor). THE PORT fires whenever the level has a torch (Game.cpp
hasTorch), and against a LIT one Torch's toggle puts it out and brings the light
wall back - the reverse of the original's help. A gameplay divergence, filed for the
owner (planning step 99), not built.
Then elapsedTime = 0, state FIGHTING, and the Follower forced to the angle it holds.
darkDragonOvertimeSmallExplosionAdder runs every DAMAGE update too (ins 1558-1563): not
built (not_built).

its own point, the angle it holds   -> shout+fallMove, angle + 30          3000 ms
shout+fallMove, angle + 30          -> shout+fallMove+(0,256), angle + 30  6000 ms
(terminal)
Each update (ins 1775-1842): SetEmissiveColor(waypoint colour) - WHITE, so the dying
dragon is drawn at full brightness whatever the room's light - SetAngle(waypoint
angle), and the jaw shut over the first leg, clamp(uint(smoothBeginning(1 - bias) x
14), 0, 3). darkDragonOvertimeSmallExplosionAdder every update (397662..398213: a
random direction, scale(64) * (randF(0.7)+0.4), an over-time
small_explosion_no_light.ent) is not built.
AT THE LAST WAYPOINT it adds key.ent at `key_pos` - AddScaledEntity at key_pos's own

The key is drawn as the key.ent it is, bobbing while it lies, as the ghost's is.
THE KEY IS THE LEVEL'S LOCK. level31c places keyhole.ent and door_locked.ent both
`yellow` and places NO key of its own - so the only key in the level is the one this
boss drops, and the fight IS the lock, exactly as it is for the ghost in level31b. The
colour is carried here because the key is created at run time and so has no node to
read it from.
_platform_note: THE PLATFORM THE DEATH ADDS IS BUILT NOW, and it was a GAP rather than a flourish.
The original adds a single_block_plat_no_emissive.ent at `platform_pos` (160, 240) as
the dragon falls. This port could not: LevelBuilder::BuildEntity builds a NODE the
scene holds and none stands at that marker - the original makes the body from the .ent
itself. LevelBuilder::BuildStaticBox is that missing road, and DarkDragon::Turn now
carries the flag it refused to carry while Game could not act on it.
NEITHER ITS SIZE NOR ITS PICTURE IS WRITTEN DOWN HERE, and deliberately. level31c
places THREE single_block_plat_no_emissive nodes of its own, so the first is kept as a
template: LevelBuilder::ShapeBoundsPx gives the box from its CollisionPolygon2D (64 x
32, the polygon running x -32..32 and y -16..16) and the layer borrows its Sprite2D
texture. entities/ holds the .ent and NO .png for this entity, so a picture could not
have been loaded by name in any case.
WHY IT MATTERS, which playing settled. level31c's floor at y=240 is light_wall 126x30
platform_no_emissive 256x32 twice -> x 256..768. The light wall carries
metadata/breakable and lighting the torch takes it away - and the torch MUST be lit to
summon this boss - so once the fight starts there is no floor at all from x 0 to 192.
The key drops at (78, 208), inside that hole. This platform spans x 128..192: the
bridge from where the wall was to where the standing floor starts. Without it the key
is on the far side of a pit, and since step 36 gave the port a level edge, a player who
goes for it falls out of the world and dies rather than falling for ever.

_source: addEntityIfItCantBeFound, called by ETHCallback_dark_dragon at ins 997-1021 (bytes
389418..397662), INSIDE the branch a shot at the player leaves by: after the sight gate
(ins 897-911, the closest contact the character), addFireball (ins 978), startEarthquake(15)
(ins 980-982) and elapsedTime = 0 (ins 984-993). So it runs once per shot at the player,
never on a tick the sight gate refuses (the clock is not reset there and the dragon asks
again next tick), never with DAMAGE's torch shot (ins 1615-1720, another branch), and never
while the level is finished (the whole block is under !isFinished, ins 821-827). Its
arguments, pushed last first (00_order 8.0 rule 3): ins 997 'barrel_bomb' (alternativeName),
457542..458062; sim/Restock.hpp has both): SeekEntity('barrel_bomb') - an exact name
compare (ETHBucketManager.cpp:394-406), which level31c's placed barrel answers (its
EntityName is bare `barrel_bomb`) and an added one answers by its alternativeName - and
only when it finds none, ghost_utility_spawn.ent and then barrel_bomb.ent, both at
barrel_spawn's GetPosition() at angle 0. A barrel asked to go off but not yet gone is
still found. Then ins 1038-1063: on the barrel it added (not null), SetVector3
('minEmissive', V3_ONE), the floor of ETHCallback_barrel_bomb's blink (#1-30,
blinkEmissive) - which the port does not draw for any barrel (not_built).
_template_note: THE PORT'S, NOT THE ORIGINAL'S: the placed entity whose node the port builds the added
barrel_bomb.ent from, because the simulation reads no .ent (sim/Restock.hpp). A bare name
and its .ent can differ (docs/ethanon-formats.md 4.5), so this is checked field by field
against the original's entities/barrel_bomb.ent (read in place, never copied): Collision
22 x 29 at Scale 1.3 -> 28.6 x 37.7, which is level31c's barrel_bomb_2225 shape
EmissiveColor 0.45, applyLight 1: its Sprite2D and eth_ keys; type 0, static 0: a
RigidBody2D; CustomData explosive 1 and teleportable 1: its metadata. The one difference
is the .ent's friction 0.7, which the port does not read for any rigid body (every one
is built at LevelBuilder's kBodyFriction 1, a convention that predates this step). The
node's minEmissive "" is the blink's floor, not drawn. barrel_spawn (430, 0) carries
no z, as barrel_bomb_2225 carries none.

from the level's start, gated on the light, where the port counts it from the light.
The two frames the original draws it at the spawn's z 8 (look's note).
